summary: Streaming handshake latency amplification leading to elevated 5xx wave across API gateway and downstream runtimes
description:
Issue summary:
Between ~03:10–03:35 UTC on 2026-03-13 we observed a rapid increase in 5xx responses for short-lived streaming sessions for a subset of dedicated customers. The spike originated at the API gateway and propagated to serving runtimes which reported OOMKills and heavy connection churn.

Impact:
- ~12% 5xx rate for streaming endpoints for affected tenants (baseline ~0.3%)
- Several customer streaming sessions failed to establish or were terminated with 502/503/504
- Increased p95 end-to-end latency for streaming connect (from ~120ms to ~900ms)
- Large dedicated customer (AcmeAI) experienced degraded UX for timeboxed inference jobs

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1) dedicated capacity pool for AcmeAI
- API Gateway + TLS terminator in front of edge proxies -> runtime pool running redwood/gptx-13b-v2

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Many short-lived streaming connects (client-side: websockets or HTTP/2) begin concurrently (traffic burst or tenant warmup).
2) TLS negotiation for a subset of connections falls back to slower cipher/path after initial cipher negotiation fails (seen in TLS debug traces).
3) Handshake stalls keep connections in accept/handshake state longer than normal, causing accept queue growth on API gateway and edge proxies.
4) Edge proxies begin to queue requests, upstream keepalive reuse saturates leading to connection churn and duplicate half-open handshakes.
5) Serving runtimes see burst of simultaneous new sessions, K/V cache thrashing, and transient memory pressure leading to OOMKills and restarts.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway metrics: accept queue depth spike, SYN retransmits, TLS handshake time p95 from ~30ms to 1.2s
- Runtime metrics: memory spikes, OOMKilled events on 3/8 pods in the dedicated pool, model prefetch cancellations
- Logs: repeated "TLS handshake timeout" and "connection reset during handshake" sequences, runtime logs show "alloc failure -> OOMKill" and subsequent restart backoffs

Expected behavior:
- Short handshake times, low accept queue/zero backlog, runtime keepalive reuse without thrash, stable OOM-free pods during tenant warmup
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Coordinate a short-lived streaming burst from a test tenant (2000 parallel short connects within 5 minutes).
2) Observe api-gateway accept queue and tls-terminator handshake timings.
3) Inspect edge proxy keepalive reuse and runtime pod memory metrics.
4) Collect tcpdump/tls debug traces on one edge node and one runtime pod during the burst.
Note: test must be in dedicated pool with similar scale to AcmeAI traffic pattern.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Ava Martinez, Diego Chen):
- Correlated API gateway accept/backlog metrics with timing of customer traffic increase.
- TLS debug traces show a non-trivial fraction (~7%) of incoming connects entering a fallback negotiation flow that increases handshake time ~20x. This correlates strongly with accept queue growth.
- Edge proxy connection reuse appears to be less effective under these long-handshake conditions, causing new TCP sessions and more TLS work.
- Serving runtimes received a concentrated burst of new session establishments once handshakes completed; this coincided with K/V cache invalidation spikes and pod memory pressure.
- Hypothesis: fallback/negotiation path (possibly triggered by a rare client cipher ordering or a bug in the TLS library on the terminator) created a timing amplification loop: longer handshakes -> accept queue growth -> connection churn -> runtime burst -> OOMs -> increased 5xx.

What we've collected so far:
- Api-gateway p50/p95/p99 handshake durations
- Edge tcpdump segments + TLS debug for 12 sample failed connections (attached)
- Runtime pod OOM stack traces and memory charts
- Customer request IDs and example session IDs (sent to AcmeAI for correlation)

Open questions:
- Is the fallback triggered by a particular client TLS fingerprint (AcmeAI SDK version?)
- Did a recent infra change (TLS library upgrade or ciphers config) coincide with this?
- Why does the runtime memory pressure align so tightly — is there a prefetch inflation bug when many sessions establish close together?
comments: 2026-03-13 04:05 - Diego Chen (SRE): Spin up additional standby runtime pods in the dedicated pool as temporary buffer. Action: autoscale override + manual warmup. Status: done at 04:12.

2026-03-13 04:22 - Support (Ava Martinez): Reached out to AcmeAI to request SDK logs and whether they pushed an SDK release at 03:00 UTC. Customer replied they did a minor SDK update at 02:58 (version 1.4.7 -> 1.4.8) and will send logs.

2026-03-13 05:00 - Diego Chen: Applied temporary apigw accept-queue hard limit to shed new handshakes beyond 400 and enabled early TLS timeout at 800ms. Initial effect: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 4% within 10m.

2026-03-13 06:20 - Infra (Maya Patel): Found that TLS library (libtls-2.3.0) was rolled to edge nodes on 2026-03-10; 2.3.1 includes a known fallback-change ticket. Opening INT-4589 to confirm behavior.
2026-03-13 08:45 - Support: Customer confirmed SDK 1.4.8 sends a legacy cipher order in certain environments; they are reverting to 1.4.7 for immediate mitigation.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Diego Chen: Running controlled repro in staging with SDK 1.4.8 showed reproducible handshake fallback and similar accept queue behavior. Working on a patch and configuration rollback plan.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: manually increased dedicated warm pool capacity and enabled early TLS handshake timeout at the gateway; AcmeAI reverted to SDK 1.4.7 which eliminated the client-side trigger in customer traffic.
Longer-term next steps:
- Infra to evaluate TLS terminator config and consider pinning accepted cipher suites to avoid fallback path (PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1952).
- Patch to runtime prefetch/backoff logic to avoid simultaneous heavy prefetch on rapid connect storms (ENG-2231).
- Follow-up action: coordinate with AcmeAI to run upgraded SDK in a canary with instrumented handshake traces.
Status: mitigation reduced impact; final remediation in progress (target: rolling config + runtime fix by 2026-03-20).
resolution_status_notes: Partial mitigation successful; customer impact reduced. Engineering to deliver permanent fix; support to schedule postmortem and notify SLA team if credit warranted.
